title: Amortized latency per session bench - exploratory
content:
Summary:

This is an exploratory doc capturing a small set of session-oriented microbenchmarks that measure amortized latency and cost-per-session for interactive conversational workloads. Goal: quantify how much latency and token-cost can be amortized by reusing KV cache across turns, by batching within session windows, and by varying session length distributions. Not a polished report — mostly raw observations, ASCII tables, and open questions for the next run.

Test harness / environment:
- Hardware: 1xA100-80GB and 1xH100-80GB nodes (single-GPU runs), single model per GPU; separate runs for each GPU type.
- Runtime: rw-infer 0.9.3 (local dev build) with KV cache enabled; small reclaim window disabled.
- Models: redwood/70B-qat (fp16, q4f16), redwood/13B-std (fp16), redwood/7B-int8 (int8).
- Workload driver: synthetic session driver that samples conversation length from distribution (see below), sends turns with average 40 tokens per user turn, 80 tokens per assistant turn. Inter-turn idle gap: 500ms to mimic typing.
- Batching modes: none (single request), intra-session microbatching (collect up to 50ms or up to 4 concurrent turns for same session), cross-session batching (batching across different sessions up to batch size 16).
- KV cache hit behavior: warm vs cold session defined below.

Session definitions / distributions:
- Short sessions: geometric( p=0.5 ) => mean ~2 turns (user+assistant = 2 exchange pairs)
- Medium sessions: geometric( p=0.2 ) => mean ~5 turns
- Long sessions: fixed 20 turns
- Mixed distribution: 50% short, 30% medium, 20% long (intended to approximate casual chat mix).

Metrics captured per session:
- p50, p95, p99 end-to-end latency from client-send to assistant-token-end (ms)
- amortized latency per-turn (session total latency / number of turns)
- cost-per-session (GPU-minutes converted to $ using internal cost model, includes idle KV state amortization)
- tokens per session (input + output)
- KV cache size and reuse (fraction of KV reused across turns)

Raw results (selected slices). Note: numbers are illustrative of relative trends, not absolute production numbers.

1) Medium sessions (mean ~5 turns), redwood/13B-std on A100

Latency vs batching mode:
Mode                     | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | amortized latency/turn(ms) | cost/session ($)
-------------------------+---------+---------+---------+----------------------------+------------------
No batching (single)     | 320     | 680     | 980     | 520                        | 0.017            
Intra-session microbatch | 260     | 540     | 800     | 350                        | 0.013            
Cross-session batch(8)   | 420     | 900     | 1300    | 300                        | 0.010            

Notes: cross-session batching reduces amortized latency/turn because throughput is higher (cost/session lowers to $0.01) but increases tail latency substantially for individual requests. Intra-session microbatching gives a good SLO tradeoff: p95 improves and amortized latency drops without catastrophic p99 inflation.

2) Long sessions (20 turns), redwood/70B-qat on H100

Warm session (KV warm from first turn) vs Cold start:
Type     | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | amortized latency/turn(ms) | cost/session ($) | kv_reuse_fraction
---------+---------+---------+---------+----------------------------+------------------+------------------
Cold     | 1200    | 2350    | 3200    | 2100                       | 0.38             | 0.00
Warm     | 880     | 1400    | 1900    | 520                        | 0.35             | 0.74

Interpretation: long sessions gain huge amortization benefits from KV reuse — amortized latency per turn drops ~75% when warm. Absolute session cost changes modestly (model compute dominates), but per-turn cost falls significantly. Warm sessions show consistent p99 reduction but p99 still high for 70B when sequences are long.

3) Short sessions (mean 2 turns), redwood/7B-int8 on A100

Mode | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | amortized latency/turn(ms) | cost/session ($)
-----+---------+---------+---------+----------------------------+------------------
Single | 180   | 420     | 780     | 300                        | 0.005            
Batch4  | 260   | 620     | 1000    | 180                        | 0.004            

Observation: For short sessions, cross-session batching helps unit economics but hurts tail latency for some requests. If product SLOs care about p99, need to cap cross-session batch sizes or prefer intra-session microbatching.

4) Mixed distribution (50/30/20) — combined system-level view (70B & 13B proportions tuned to match 30% heavy users)

Metric             | Value
-------------------+----------------
Average session length (turns) | 4.6
Average tokens/session          | 460
Average amortized latency/turn  | 420 ms
System p95 (across sessions)    | 1100 ms
Avg cost/session                | $0.053

Short notes on cost model: cost/session includes an allocation of daemon memory and KV storage for the session on the GPU for the expected session lifetime (idle expiry after 60s). We charged idle KV memory proportionally to session length to approximate customer-visible unit economics for session-based product pricing.

ASCII chart (amortized latency per turn vs session length in turns)
Session length (turns) -> amortized latency (ms)
1  : 600
2  : 350
5  : 220
10 : 130
20 : 75

(Chart shows steep amortization curve: first few turns recover most of the cold-start cost)

Key takeaways:
- KV cache reuse is the dominant driver of amortized latency gains for medium+ sessions; long sessions get >3x per-turn improvements when warm.
- Cross-session batching reduces cost/session but increases p99 latency; acceptable for background throughput workloads but risky for low-SLO interactive paths.
- Intra-session microbatching (short delay window 20–50ms) gives good tradeoffs for interactive applications: reduces amortized latency and cost without extreme tail inflation.
- Idle expiry (session keepalive window) tuning materially affects cost estimates; longer keepalive helps UX (warm starts) but increases idle-cost amortized across sessions.

Open questions / next runs:
- Run systematic sweep for idle expiry windows (10s, 30s, 60s, 180s) and measure cost/session vs perceived latency improvement distribution.
- Add network variability to client-to-proxy leg (introduce 50–200ms jitter) to see how much server-side batching helps hide network noise.
- Include a small production trace sample to calibrate session length distribution (we used synthetic distributions).
- Evaluate memory-pressure eviction scenarios: how often do we drop KV for long sessions under mixed load?
- Probe quantization impact on tail latency for long contexts (70B-qat vs 70B-std).

Recommended short-term actions:
1) Prototype intra-session microbatching as an opt-in flag for chat route (20–40ms window). Add telemetry to measure p95/p99 changes live.
2) Expose session keepalive as a config knob in Redwood Console per route, and surface estimated incremental cost per minute.
3) Add a dashboard plot: amortized latency per turn vs session length with sliders for keepalive and batching mode.

Notes to self / quick TODOs:
- Re-run long-session 70B on A100 to compare against H100 numbers (we only ran 70B on H100 in this pass).
- Add a run with cross-model routing (start on 7B for first turns, route to 70B on long-turn escalation) and measure combined amortized cost.
- Share with Maya and SRE for feedback on microbatch window sizing.

End of draft.
